context: To show that Algorithm 2 is also corruption-resilient, one may apply [38, Lemma 1.8], which essentially says an error-resilient algorithm that has probability at most 1/3 to either err or see a manipulation, is also corruption-resilient. For the soundness, our analysis holds since it suffices to have one iteration that finds a witness without seeing manipulations. For completeness, note that the algorithm can only err if it has seen a manipulation, and the probability of seeing a manipulation at any iteration is at most 3α/25 by Lemma 3.2.
